analyzed_vuln.description: HashContext object unserialization accepts attacker-controlled internal hash state values (including xxh64 state fields) without validating invariants. The crafted state makes XXH64_update compute an invalid huge copy length (size_t underflow/overflow), leading to out-of-bounds read in XXH_memcpy during hash_update(). Crash manifests in XXH64_update/PHP_XXH64Update, but root cause is unsafe deserialization in php_hash_unserialize().
analyzed_vuln.conditions: In harness php-fuzz-unserializehash, input after '|' is unserialized into a HashContext object. If algorithm is xxh64 and internal state array elements are forged (as in PoC), then fuzzer calls hash_update(HashContext, prefix-data). hash_update passes a small zend string buffer to xxh64 update, which trusts corrupted state and performs memcpy with a massive length, causing heap-buffer-overflow read. Requires successful creation of HashContext via unserialize with malicious state and subsequent hash_update call.
